question: Should OpenClaw extend its generic embedding and memory-index contracts for document-group contextual embeddings, or keep this capability entirely inside external memory plugins?
rationale: The current plugin contract does not fully express grouped document chunks or index-generation migration, while adding provider-specific native behavior would conflict with the repository's lean-core ownership direction.

options.title: Extend generic contracts first
options.body: Design typed contextual document/query embedding capabilities plus generic index identity, cutover, status, and rollback semantics before adding a Voyage provider implementation.

options.title: Keep it external
options.body: Keep native memory on ordinary embeddings and direct contextual providers to full memory plugins distributed through ClawHub.

options.title: Add Voyage-specific native mode
options.body: Implement the requested behavior directly in memory-core and accept provider-specific config, storage, migration, and diagnostics complexity.

recommendation.title: Extend generic contracts first
recommendation.body: Design typed contextual document/query embedding capabilities plus generic index identity, cutover, status, and rollback semantics before adding a Voyage provider implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to the core-versus-plugin memory scope and current vision guidance.
